newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND-BASED HOOKER BILLUPS BREAKS HIS NECK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND-BASED HOOKER BILLUPS BREAKS HIS NECK.

text.p: HONG KONG, May 17, Reuter - American Tom Billups, who plays for English club Harlequins, broke his neck during a match between the United States and Hong Kong on Saturday and will be out of the game for up to five months.
Billups, the most capped hooker for the U.S., was injured when the scrum buckled near the end of the Pacific Rim championship match which Hong Kong won 46-9.

"He has a fracture of the neck but it is not catastrophic," said Hong Kong team doctor Mike Fleming. "There is no spinal cord damage and no paralysis. He will be kept in hospital overnight but should be able to fly back to San Francisco with the United States team doctor tomorrow evening.
"He will be out of rugby for up to five months but he is already talking of getting fit for future matches with the United States."

The victory took Hong Kong to the top of the standings in the four-team tournament following their 42-20 victory over Japan two weeks ago. Canada, who beat the United States 53-14 last weekend, play Japan in Osaka on Sunday.
